challenge.method: Compared both Index decisions for the same opaque entity and edition. Tested substitution of the earlier bilingual HTML for the Markdown and checked whether the comparison to CC0 indicated a shared identity.
challenge.results: The inherited row uses sha256:942ff5fea9ce6e3184ff7c6134f259b06f901200211815e6ddd8ab7392254168. Its matching name and active value cannot establish the Markdown revision. The separate reaffirmation binds the Markdown digest explicitly and preserves the HTML decision in history. GovData lists CC0 as a comparable alternative. Neither comparison creates a contradiction for this identity.

limitations: The English canonical name is the Index rendering of the German title. The Markdown quotes a German excerpt. The complete bilingual licence and the exact deployed site version require separate evidence.

Active means the Index maintains the reference for current lookup after selection. Publisher currency, SPDX deprecation, application to a particular work, redistribution rights, installation eligibility and dataset release authorization require separate evidence.
reasoning: GovData’s German edition document names Datenlizenz Deutschland – Zero – Version 2.0, describes it as an open licence, and links to the original licence page. The repository README establishes the document’s GovData publication lineage. The Index admits this instrument as a license and expressly reaffirms active for the exact Markdown revision.
